title: Meopham air disaster
summary: A Junkers F.13ge chartered by Walcot Air Line crashed near Meopham, Kent, on July 21, 1930. Witnesses reported a rumbling noise before the aircraft emerged from cloud and broke apart in mid-air. The port tailplane failed under severe buffeting from air eddies, causing the aircraft to enter a dive. Flutter effects on the starboard tailplane caused it to fail next, and the port wing broke away at high speed, killing all six occupants.
probable_cause: The failure of the tailplane under severe buffeting from air eddies produced by the centre section of the low-wing monoplane when the aircraft approached the stalling attitude.

factors.evidence: The port tailplane failed under severe buffeting from air eddies produced by the centre section when the aircraft approached the stalling attitude.
The aircraft was flying in clouds when it was thrown into an unusual attitude.
The aircraft was moving at high speed and reached a stalling attitude, causing the port wing to break away.
The failure of the tailplane under severe buffeting from air eddies produced by the centre section of the aircraft when it approached the stalling attitude.

events.text: Aircraft was flying in clouds above Kent with six occupants including pilot Lieutenant-Colonel George Henderson.
Witnesses reported a rumbling noise just before the crash.
Aircraft emerged from cloud and the port wing had folded or collapsed upwards where it joined the fuselage.
Aircraft disintegrated with the engine and tail plane broken away; all six occupants fell from aircraft or were killed in the wreckage.

title: R101 airship disaster
summary: The R101 airship disaster resulted in 48 deaths.

events.text: The R101 airship experienced a catastrophic structural failure.
